newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup confirms wants to sell US hotels.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup confirms wants to sell US hotels.

text.p: SAirGroup, the holding company for the Swissair airline and Swissotel hotel chain, said its four hotels in the United States had been for sale for some time, but it could not confirm the prices being asked.
"The intention has been to sell the four hotels that we own in the U.S. for some time," said a SAirGroup spokesman.
"The strategy of Swissotel is to expand, but not by owning hotels and thus tie up capital," he said, adding Swissotel aimed to expand by reaching management agreements.

The Boston Business Journal on Friday quoted Robert Webster, executive vice president of Hodges Ward Elliot Inc. that Swissotel is asking around $465 millionm for its four properties in Boston, Atlanta, Chicago and New York.
The paper said Hodges Ward Elliot was brokering the sale.

Earlier this month Swissotel managing director Andreas Meinhold said in an interview with SAirGroup's internal magazine that Swissotel planned to manage more than 20 hotels by the end of 1997 up from the current 16.
By year 2000 Meinhold said he wanted to have 60 hotels under management in Asia, the Middle East, Europe and the U.S.
Meinhold added Swissotel would reach this goal through a strategic alliance, for example with a medium-sized partner that has 30 to 40 hotels.
